content.title: About
content.content: Basil is an aromatic annual herb from the Lamiaceae family. Fresh leaves are bright green, highly fragrant, and have a mildly peppery flavor. Basil is widely used in cooking, cosmetics, and traditional medicine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Basil originates from tropical and subtropical regions of Asia but is now cultivated worldwide.
There are more than 60 varieties, including Genovese, Thai, and Lemon basil.
In ancient Roman mythology basil was a symbol of love and prosperity.
Basil seeds are used as a spice and in aromatherapy.
Basil wilts quickly after harvest, so it is usually consumed fresh.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Leaves contain essential oils, flavonoids, and vitamin C, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Compounds such as eugenol and carvacrol stimulate bile production and aid digestion.

items.title: Anti‑inflammatory properties
items.content: Basil exhibits moderate anti‑inflammatory effects that can be helpful during colds.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is important for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Fresh basil is virtually calorie‑free, making it a great addition to weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to basil, such as skin itching or swelling.

items.title: Drug interactions
items.content: Because of its high vitamin K content, basil may enhance the effects of anticoagulant medications.

items.title: Contamination risk
items.content: Fresh leaves can be contaminated with pesticides or bacteria, so they should be washed thoroughly before use.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use fresh basil in salads, sauces (pesto), soups, marinades, and as a garnish. Leaves can be sliced, blended, or added whole to hot dishes at the end of cooking to preserve their aroma.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh basil in the refrigerator in a sealed container with a damp paper towel for 3‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze the leaves or make pesto and freeze in portioned bags.
